CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication side effects.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a modest improvement in his anxiety symptoms since the last visit. He states that while the sertraline continues to provide daytime anxiety relief, he is experiencing increased drowsiness during the day, which he attributes to the recent addition of amitriptyline for headache prophylaxis. He reports that he has been taking amitriptyline 10 mg nightly for the past month, which has resulted in a decrease in the frequency of his tension-type headaches to 2 to 3 times per week; however, he is concerned about the persistent fatigue and sedation he feels during the day.
Sleep quality has not significantly improved, as Mr. Smith still averages around 5 hours of sleep per night and continues to wake multiple times. He has been diligent in practicing CBT-I techniques but finds it increasingly difficult to manage his sleep hygiene due to ongoing work stress and the sedative effects of amitriptyline. He expresses frustration regarding his persistent fatigue, which he feels is compounded by the side effects of his medications and the stressors at work.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 100 mg daily 2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and has maintained his walking routine three times a week. He reports that he has been more consistent with his stretching exercises, which he finds beneficial. He continues to consume alcohol socially but has reduced his intake due to concerns about its impact on his sleep. He remains engaged in mindfulness meditation sessions and has recently started practicing guided imagery techniques to further manage his stress.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports ongoing anxiety, persistent sleep disturbances, increased daytime sedation, no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Tension-type headaches as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with ongoing anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline 100 mg daily; consider referral to a psychiatrist for evaluation of potential dose adjustment or alternative therapy if no significant improvement is noted by the next visit. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin 3 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies and sleep hygiene practices. Discuss the possibility of reducing amitriptyline to 5 mg nightly to mitigate daytime sedation while monitoring headache control. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen 400 mg as needed; evaluate headache frequency and intensity at the next visit to determine the need for further prophylactic treatment. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage ongoing physical activity and mindfulness practices; assess for any underlying sleep disorders if fatigue persists despite medication adjustments.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-02-01 to evaluate symptoms, treatment effectiveness, and medication side effects. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or side effects from medications.
